title: stale-session-cookie-causing-tenant-metering-leak
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Intermittent billing spikes observed for a handful of customers after an edge gateway deployment. Initial signal: sudden increase in token counts attributed to unrelated projects within same org. Hypothesis: an edge-level session cookie used by the legacy gateway can expire out-of-sync with downstream tenant bindings, causing some requests to be stamped with a stale workspace id and double-counted by metering pipeline.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy the edge gateway with the sticky-session cookie enabled (X-Edge-Session) with TTL 24h
2) Rotate API keys for a test sub-account while session cookie still valid
3) Replay traffic from client that retains old cookie header but supplies new API key in Authorization header
4) Observe that the request is accepted, but the attribution resolver uses the cached session cookie workspace_id instead of authoritative API key binding
5) Verify metering pipeline shows tokens attributed to the stale workspace_id and rate limiter counters increment for the wrong project
root_cause_summary: A race between edge session affinity and the API key rotation flow. The edge cache persisted an association (cookie -> workspace_id) longer than downstream auth caches were invalidated. When API keys were rotated, the control plane updated project bindings but the edge continued to stamp the old workspace_id. Metering and rate-limiter components trust the stamped workspace_id for attribution, leading to ghost counts on the old project and missing counts on the new one.
proposed_fix: 1) Short-term: turn off sticky session cookie behavior at the gateway for any tenant-bound cookies; implement a hard TTL of 5 minutes for session-to-workspace mapping and invalidate on key rotation events. 2) Medium-term: change attribution precedence so that API key -> workspace resolution is authoritative and overrides any edge-stamped cookie when Authorization header is present. 3) Add a background reconciliation job to scan recent tokens and reassign misattributed counts where strong evidence exists.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): deploy gateway config change to us-west-2 small fleet for 1 hour with increased tracing. Phase B: if no regressions, roll to all gateways over 2 hours. Phase C: deploy attribution precedence change to metering service behind a feature flag, enable for 10% of traffic, validate. Phase D: full enable + reconciliation job run. Include rollback gateway toggle to restore previous cookie behavior.
monitoring_and_mitigation: Create dashboard showing per-workspace delta between API-key-derived counts and edge-stamped counts. Add alert: >5% mismatch sustained for 10m. Rate-limiter to apply defensive caps to prevent runaway billing while we reconcile. Enable request-level tracing for any rotated-key events for 72 hours post-rollout.
risk_and_rollback: Risk: changing attribution precedence could temporarily undercount if services downstream rely on edge-stamped workspace id. Rollback plan: re-enable cookie behavior and disable precedence change feature flag. Reconciliation job is reversible — do not persist changes until reconciliation is reviewed by Billing team.
